text:
### Śrīmad Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa in the Yuddha Kāṇḍa <note>The Book of War</note>

730

Bears, lions, boars, buffaloes, elephants, and deer were terrified by that sound and fled in fear in all ten directions. There was a single lofty peak of Mount Trikūṭa that touched the heavens; it was covered everywhere with flowers and shone like great silver. 18

It was one hundred <term>yojanas</term> <gloss>a measurement of distance, approximately eight miles</gloss> wide, pure and beautiful to behold. It was smooth, majestic, and immense, unreachable even by birds. 19

It was difficult to climb even in one's mind, let alone by the actions of men. Built upon that peak was the city of Laṅkā, ruled by Rāvaṇa. 20

The city was one hundred <term>yojanas</term> long and thirty <term>yojanas</term> wide. It possessed tall gate-towers that resembled white clouds. 21

It was adorned with a golden wall and decorated with silver. Laṅkā was highly embellished with palaces and <term>vimānas</term> <gloss>celestial mansions or flying chariots</gloss>. 22

It looked like the middle path of Viṣṇu <note>the sky</note> when covered with clouds at the end of the summer heat. There, a palace adorned with a thousand pillars was visible. 23

Resembling a peak of Mount Kailāsa, it seemed to scrape the sky. This <term>caitya</term> <gloss>sacred monument or palace shrine</gloss> of the Lord of Rākṣasas was the jewel of the city. 24

It was guarded constantly by a full hundred Rākṣasas. It had beautiful forests and was graced by mountains. 25

The city was beautified by gardens varied with various minerals, filled with the cries of different birds and inhabited by diverse animals. 26

It was covered with various flowers and inhabited by various Rākṣasas <note>This half-verse is missing in some versions</note>. The glorious Rāma, the elder brother of Lakṣmaṇa, together with the Vānaras, beheld that prosperous city of Rāvaṇa which was full of wealth. Having seen that city crowded with great houses, the heroic elder brother of Lakṣmaṇa was filled with wonder. 27–28

Rāma, along with his great army, gazed upon that city filled with jewels, containing many arrangements, adorned with rows of palaces, and featuring great mechanical gateways. 29

Thus ends the thirty-ninth <term>sarga</term> <gloss>canto</gloss>, named The Sight of Laṅkā, in the Yuddha Kāṇḍa of the glorious Rāmāyaṇa of Vālmīki, the first ever poem, a compendium of twenty-four thousand verses.

---

### Canto 40
**The Duel between Rāvaṇa and Sugrīva**

Then Rāma, along with Sugrīva and surrounded by the leaders of the Vānara troops, ascended the summit of Mount Suvela, which was two <term>yojanas</term> in circumference. 1

Standing there for a moment and looking in all ten directions, he saw Laṅkā, built by Viśvakarman <note>the divine architect</note> on the lovely peak of Trikūṭa, well-laid out and graced by beautiful forests. 2–3

He saw the Lord of Rākṣasas, difficult to approach, standing on the top of a gate-tower. He was flanked by white whisks and graced by a victory umbrella. 4

He was anointed with red sandalwood and adorned with jeweled ornaments. Resembling a dark rain-cloud, he wore garments embroidered with gold. 5

His chest bore scars inflicted by the tips of the tusks of Airāvata <note>Indra's elephant</note>. He was wrapped in a red cloth with the hue of a rabbit's blood. 6

He appeared like a mass of clouds in the sky enveloped by the light of the evening sun. While the Vānara leaders were looking and while Rāma was also looking, Sugrīva, upon seeing the Lord of Rākṣasas, suddenly rose up. 7

<margin>This half-verse is not in the "ka" manuscript.</margin>

<summary>Rāma and the Vānara army view the magnificent city of Laṅkā from Mount Suvela. Sugrīva reacts impulsively upon spotting Rāvaṇa standing atop his city's fortifications.</summary>
<keywords>Lanka, Rāvaṇa, Rāma, Sugrīva, Trikūṭa, Suvela, architecture, Rākṣasa</keywords>
